actions.label: Assign guards and militia to organise distribution block by block
Ensure equal distribution to all refugees and end collective punishment
Allow FWB to consult refugees and communicate publicly without camp clearance
Give FWB staff independent, unescorted movement inside the camp
Order generator parts and press SML/Ministry of Defense for fuel funding
Permit and facilitate FWB's nutritional assessment with security arrangements
Accept coordinated, escorted camp access without free movement
Commit to an ongoing, scheduled food aid supply to the camp
Hand distribution to existing guard and militia structures
Include compensated militia men in distribution roles alongside FWB staff
Provide food rations or in-kind payment to guards and their families
Distribute food equally to all registered refugees

goals.label: Ongoing, reliable food aid supply to the camp
Aid accountability and documentation meeting FWB and donor requirements
Camp generators kept running with fuel and repairs
Camp guards and militia control food distribution
Commander's authority and image of strength over the camp
Commander's control over information and narrative about the camp
Commander's personal safety and legal exposure
Commander's standing with the SML and militia demands met
FWB neutrality and impartiality toward camp operators and armed actors
FWB staff have independent access and movement inside the camp
FWB's reputation and public profile
Food aid diverted or skimmed by guards, militia or officials
Food distributed equally to all refugees, including those labelled terrorists
Government and Ministry of Defense funding for camp operations
Guards and their families are fed and paid, keeping them loyal
Refugees receive adequate food and nutrition
Refugees remain contained in the camp, away from the capital
Refugees subjected to abuse or collective punishment by guards
Safety of FWB staff and local hires from threats and violence
Security risks from outsiders moving freely in the camp
Visible abuse or unrest drawing international attention and political cost
Accurate independent information on refugees' nutritional needs
Refugees' voices heard in aid design and delivery

redLines.label: Allow FWB staff and FWB-chosen assistants to manage food distribution, with guards limited to security
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
